steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Primary processing converts raw food materials into basic ingredients: milling wheat into flour, pasteurising milk, refining sugar cane, and slaughtering and butchering animals. | Key Fact: Secondary processing converts primary-processed ingredients into more complex products: making flour into bread, milk into cheese, flour and sugar into biscuits, potatoes into crisps. | Key Fact: Food additives are substances added to food for a specific purpose: preservatives (extend shelf life), colourants (improve appearance), flavourings (enhance taste), emulsifiers (mix oil and water), stabilisers (maintain texture). | Key Fact: Additives are given E numbers when approved for use in the EU; some consumers prefer additive-free foods due to health concerns (e.g. hyperactivity linked to some
